The Show-Ready Sale

Six steps. You're only needed for the first one.

  1. 01

    The walk-through

    Jack walks your house and gives you two honest numbers: what it's worth as-is, and what it's worth show-ready. Then he tells you exactly which repairs and upgrades earn their money back — and which ones to skip. No pressure toward either path.

  2. 02

    He runs the work

    Say yes, and Jack gathers the bids and puts his own contractors, cleaners, and stagers to work. He schedules them and supervises them — you don't have to be in town, or in California.

  3. 03

    Staged like a model home

    Buyers pay for what they can picture themselves living in. Your house gets the model-home treatment: staged rooms, professional photography, virtual tours, and a listing built to stop the scroll.

  4. 04

    Priced from real data

    Jack has sold roughly seventy-five homes a year here since 1988. He prices from what your street actually sells for — not a ZIP-code average — to draw strong offers in the first week, when buyer attention is highest.

  5. 05

    Marketing and showings

    Your listing goes out with professional photos across Zillow and the MLS, in front of the buyer agents Jack has worked with for decades. He handles every showing and every call. Sellers routinely never attend a single one.

  6. 06

    Escrow to sold

    Jack negotiates the offers, manages inspections and paperwork, and walks the sale to closing. From the first bid to the final signature, his is the only phone number you need.

One broker, every vendor

Contractors, cleaners, stagers, photographers, inspectors. Jack brings the whole crew.

Getting a house show-ready usually means hunting for contractors, chasing quotes, and scheduling strangers around your move. Jack does that part: he gets the bids, books the staging, the photography, and the virtual tour, and manages the inspections. If you've ever put off selling because the house "isn't ready" — this is built for you.
